record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: Does every separable Aharoni space contain a linear copy of c0? A Banach space Y is an Aharoni space when every separable Banach space is Lipschitz-isomorphic to a subspace of Y.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a Banach space $Y$ an Aharoni space if every separable Banach space is Lipschitz-isomorphic to a subset of $Y$ (that is, for every separable Banach space $X$ there exist a subset $S\subseteq Y$ and a bijection $f:X\to S$ such that both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are Lipschitz). By Aharoni's theorem, $c_0$ is an Aharoni space.

Question: Does every separable Aharoni space $Y$ necessarily contain a linear isomorphic copy of $c_0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The converse-Aharoni question — whether a (separable) Banach space into which every separable Banach space Lipschitz-embeds must contain a linear copy of $c_0$ — is discussed in surveys on nonlinear geometry of Banach spaces as a known open problem. Partial results (e.g. Kalton's theorem that coarse embeddability of $c_0$ into a separable Banach space prevents reflexivity) constrain such spaces but do not resolve the question. No published solution was located.

status_evidence.title: A short course on non linear geometry of Banach spaces (Godefroy–Kalton–Lancien)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Aharoni's theorem and open converse-type questions on Lipschitz embeddings into Banach spaces containing c_0.
status_evidence.claim: The converse Aharoni problem is presented as an open problem in surveys on nonlinear Banach space geometry.

status_evidence.title: Non Linear Geometry of Banach Spaces, G. Lancien
status_evidence.snippet: Aharoni: every separable metric space Lipschitz-embeds into c_0; converse-type questions about linear copies of c_0 are noted.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of the converse direction appears; the question is presented as unresolved.
